documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Winter check. Work slow, which means more time at home and, he admits, more drinking. Did not do the taper he talked about in the fall. Partner worried.
No bleeding, no falls. Breathing fine. Taking meds most days.
Exam: AF, rate controlled. Lungs clear. Abd soft, no ascites, no tenderness. No edema.
A/P
- AF/warfarin: INR 2.7, continue.
- HFrEF: stable, no change.
- Anemia: Hgb 12.0, best yet. Continue B6/folate.
- AUD: talked again; offered to see him more often if he wants to try cutting down. He'll think about it.
- Lung screening due next month, ordered.
RTC 3 mo.

events.reason: Sudden left upper quadrant pain, near-syncope

reports.text: Bedside abdominal ultrasound for acute left upper quadrant pain and hypotension. Free fluid in the abdomen, including the left upper quadrant and pelvis. Liver echotexture coarse. No hydronephrosis.

Specimen: spleen, splenectomy.
Gross: spleen with a 5 cm capsular tear along the lateral surface and adherent blood clot.
Microscopic: capsular disruption with acute parenchymal hemorrhage. White pulp expanded by a diffuse infiltrate of small mature lymphocytes, consistent with the patient's known chronic lymphocytic leukemia. No other neoplasm.
reports.conclusion: Spleen with capsular rupture and acute hemorrhage; involvement by known chronic lymphocytic leukemia/small lymphocytic lymphoma.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - General Surgery
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
Admit 04/05/2023 - discharge 04/11/2023
Principal diagnosis: atraumatic splenic rupture with hemoperitoneum.
Secondary: acute blood loss anemia; supratherapeutic INR on warfarin; CLL; alcoholic cirrhosis; AF; alcohol use disorder.

Presentation: 55-year-old man with heavy alcohol use, cirrhosis, CLL and AF on warfarin who developed abrupt severe left upper quadrant pain going up into the left shoulder, with lightheadedness and several near-faints. No trauma he could recall. Arrival BP 90/60, HR 120. Pale and sweaty; LUQ tender with guarding, bowel sounds present, no rebound. Hgb 8.2 (his baseline about 12), platelets 150, INR 3.5, LDH 410. Bedside ultrasound showed free fluid.

Course: warfarin reversed with IV vitamin K and 4-factor prothrombin complex concentrate; transfused packed red cells. Taken emergently for exploratory laparotomy, which found a ruptured spleen with hemoperitoneum; splenectomy performed. Pathology: capsular rupture, spleen involved by CLL. Uneventful post-op course. Monitored for alcohol withdrawal on symptom-triggered protocol, no significant withdrawal. Warfarin resumed on post-op day 5 at prior dose. Hgb 10.2 at discharge.

Discharge meds: warfarin 5 mg daily (resumed), metoprolol succinate 25 mg daily, furosemide 20 mg daily, thiamine, folic acid, pyridoxine. Short course acetaminophen for incision pain.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: PCP 1-2 weeks; post-splenectomy vaccines due 14 days after surgery (meningococcal ACWY and B, Hib; check pneumococcal status). Surgery clinic 3 weeks. INR in 1 week.

documents.title: Partner Call - Hospitalized
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Partner called: Piotr was taken to the hospital Wed night with belly pain, had emergency surgery, spleen removed. In step-down, stable. She asked us to hold his INR draw this week. Asked her to have him call when discharged to set up a visit. Records request sent.

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen 9 days after discharge. Spleen ruptured on its own on 4/5 - INR was 3.5 at the time - emergency splenectomy, transfused. Pathology shows the spleen was full of CLL. Scary for him and his partner.
Now: incision sore but healing, walking around the house, off work for 6 wks per surgery. Eating ok. Says he hasn't had a drink since the hospital.
Exam: BP and HR as recorded. Midline incision clean, staples out at surgery clinic next week. Abdomen soft. Lungs clear. AF rate 70s.
A/P
1. S/p splenectomy for atraumatic rupture: healing. Asplenia - vaccines today: MenACWY #1, MenB #1, Hib. PCV20 already done 2021. Reviewed: fever over 101 = call or go to ED same day, no waiting it out.
2. Acute blood loss anemia: Hgb 10.8 today, recovering.
3. AF on warfarin: INR 2.2. Resumed at 5 mg in hospital. Continue, close monitoring.
4. AUD: abstinent 2 wks. Encouraged; offered support, he wants to do it on his own.
RTC 2 mo. Nurse visit 5 weeks for MenB #2.

documents.title: Hematology Follow-up
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
Hematology/oncology clinic, visit 05/11/2023
CLL, observation. Acquired sideroblastic anemia, alcohol-related. S/p splenectomy 04/2023 for atraumatic rupture; spleen involved by CLL.
Recovering from surgery. No sweats, fevers or weight loss beyond the post-op period. No adenopathy.
CBC: WBC higher after splenectomy, as expected; Hgb 11.6 recovering; platelets up post-splenectomy.
Assessment: CLL without treatment indication. Post-splenectomy counts as expected.
Plan: observation. Continue pyridoxine/folic acid. Asplenia precautions and vaccines per PCP. Return 1 year.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Nurse Visit

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Recovered from splenectomy, back to full duty. Hgb back to 12.4, blood loss anemia resolved.
Alcohol: made it about 5 weeks without drinking, then back to beer "just on weekends" which has become most nights. AUDIT-C high again. Disappointed in himself.
Exam: incision well healed. Lungs clear. AF rate controlled. No edema.
A/P
- S/p splenectomy: MenACWY #2 today; series complete (MenB x2, Hib, PCV20 2021). MenACWY booster every 5 yrs.
- Posthemorrhagic anemia: resolved.
- AF/warfarin: INR in range.
- AUD: back to drinking. Talked about how close the April bleed was. Door open.
- Labs: CMP at his usual.
RTC 3-4 mo.

documents.title: Cardiology Follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group, visit 07/13/2023
AF, HFrEF (EF 30%), alcoholic and tachycardia-mediated cardiomyopathy.
Interval: splenectomy in April for spontaneous rupture with INR 3.5 on warfarin. Recovered.
Symptoms: no orthopnea or PND, mild exertional fatigue, no syncope.
Meds: metoprolol succinate 25, warfarin 5 (INR by PCP), furosemide 20.
BP 110/68, HR 76. Lungs clear, no JVD, no edema.
Plan: continue rate control and anticoagulation; benefit vs bleeding reviewed again given the April bleed and ongoing alcohol use - he wants to stay on it. Keep INR tightly in range. Follow up 1 year.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Pulmonary
documents.author: pulmonary
documents.body:
Admit 04/08/2024 - discharge 04/15/2024
Diagnosis: right lower lobe lung abscess, aspiration.

History: about three weeks of low-grade fevers, feeling unwell and a productive cough with foul-smelling sputum. Before that, a seizure at home with loss of consciousness, likely withdrawal after a short stop in drinking; he did not seek care at the time. Background: severe alcohol use disorder, cirrhosis, CLL, s/p splenectomy, AF on warfarin, HFrEF, prior aspiration pneumonias.
On arrival T 38.2 C, HR 102, RR 22, BP 135/85. Decreased breath sounds and dullness to percussion at the right base. WBC 15.0, Hgb 13.2, platelets 250, Na 135, K 4.2, BUN 18, Cr 1.0. CXR: cavitary RLL lesion.

Course: IV ampicillin-sulbactam with steady improvement; afebrile by day 4, sputum lessening. Withdrawal protocol, no further seizures. INR followed, stayed in range on warfarin with antibiotics. Transitioned to oral amoxicillin-clavulanate.

Discharge meds: amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg twice daily through 05/20/2024 (total about 6 weeks), warfarin 5 mg, metoprolol succinate 25 mg, furosemide 20 mg, thiamine, folic acid, pyridoxine.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: PCP 1 week with INR (antibiotic interaction); CT chest after antibiotics finish.

orders.reason: follow-up of RLL lung abscess after antibiotics

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Discharged 4/15 after a week for a right lower lobe lung abscess. Had a seizure at home in March - he says he'd stopped drinking for a couple of days to "dry out" and it happened then. Partner found him. Didn't go in. Three weeks later the fevers and foul sputum.
Now: no fever, cough much less, sputum clearing. Taking the amoxicillin-clavulanate twice a day, through 5/20. Stomach a little upset.
Exam: afebrile. Lungs: few crackles right base. AF rate 80. No edema.
A/P
1. RLL lung abscess, aspiration: improving on amox-clav, finish course to 5/20. CT chest after.
2. Withdrawal seizure in March: reviewed - stopping suddenly is dangerous for him; if he wants to stop, we do it with a plan and meds. He was surprised; noted.
3. AF/warfarin + antibiotic: INR 2.9, upper edge. Recheck 1 wk.
4. CBC: WBC down.
RTC after CT.

Assessment: CLL stable, no treatment indication. Anemia much improved.
Plan: observation; return 1 year. Continue pyridoxine/folic acid.
Allergies: NKDA.

reports.text:
CT chest without contrast. Indication: follow-up of right lower lobe lung abscess after treatment. Comparison: chest radiograph 04/08/2024.

Pleura: no effusion.
Heart enlarged. No mediastinal adenopathy.
Upper abdomen: nodular liver. Splenectomy.
reports.conclusion: Resolved right lower lobe lung abscess with small residual linear scar.

Indication: hematemesis after forceful retching.
Esophagus: normal mucosa; no varices. At the gastroesophageal junction, a single linear mucosal tear with mild continued oozing. One band applied across the tear with hemostasis.
Stomach: small amount of old blood, otherwise normal mucosa. No ulcer.
Duodenum: normal bulb and second portion.
reports.conclusion: Mallory-Weiss tear at the GE junction with mild oozing, treated with band ligation. No varices.

documents.title: ED and Observation Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
ED arrival 09/26/2024 01:30, observation, discharged 09/28/2024
Diagnosis: Mallory-Weiss tear.

About 2 hours of vomiting, then bright red blood, after a night of heavy drinking and hard retching. Known severe alcohol use disorder, cirrhosis, prior withdrawal seizures, AF on warfarin.
BP 110/70, pulse 98. Pale. Abdomen soft, not distended, nontender.
Hgb 13.2, Hct 39.4%, platelets 225, PT 12 s, PTT 30 s. He says he had not taken warfarin for about a week while drinking.

Urgent upper endoscopy: linear tear at the GE junction, still oozing mildly; banded with hemostasis. No varices.
Observed 2 nights: no further bleeding, Hgb stable. Withdrawal protocol, no seizure.

Discharge meds: pantoprazole 40 mg twice daily x 4 weeks (new). Hold warfarin 2 more days, then resume 5 mg daily with INR check in 1 week. Continue metoprolol, furosemide, vitamins.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: PCP 1 week.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ED/obs 9/26-9/28 for a Mallory-Weiss tear after a binge and hard retching; banded on EGD, no varices. Hadn't been taking warfarin for a week. No more bleeding since. On pantoprazole BID through ~10/26. Restarted warfarin 9/30.
Exam: not pale. Abd soft, nontender. AF rate 70s.
A/P
1. Mallory-Weiss tear: healed clinically, no further bleeding, Hgb stable. Finish PPI course.
2. AF/warfarin: INR 1.6, only 4 days back on it. Continue 5 mg, recheck 2 wks.
3. AUD: this is the third major bleed/emergency in 18 months tied to drinking. Said so plainly. He agrees and is still not ready.
4. Cirrhosis: US due next month.
5. HM: flu + COVID today.
RTC 3 mo.
